tagline: Seventeen miles east under the hardwoods, on an Ottawa chief's name.
intro: M-179 leaves US 131 at Bradley and heads east for 17 miles, around the south side of Sager Lake and into Barry County north of Gun Lake, where it becomes Chief Noonday Road. It winds through the Yankee Springs Recreation Area under a canopy of hardwoods and comes out at M-43 just west of Hastings. Until 1998 it was a county road, A-42.

Noahquageshik, the Grand River Ottawa leader called Chief Noonday, spent much of his life in what became Yankee Springs Township. He fought on Tecumseh's side at the Battle of the Thames, and when Tecumseh was killed there, Noonday inherited his tomahawk and hat.

moments.title: Bradley
moments.text: The road starts at a community founded in 1854 on the strength of a plank road being built through the area.

moments.title: Gun Lake
moments.text: The road passes north of a lake whose two halves spread on the map like the wings of a butterfly, with the recreation area on its northeastern shore.

moments.title: Yankee Springs Recreation Area
moments.text: Farmed out and eroded by the 1930s, this land was replanted by the Civilian Conservation Corps and now holds nine lakes and a glacial kettle called the Devil's Soupbowl.

sources.label: MDOT, Pure Michigan Byways Driving Guide (Wayback Machine snapshot, December 2025)
